newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK lawmakers demand report on immigration probe.
newsitem.headline: HK lawmakers demand report on immigration probe.

text.p: Hong Kong legislators probing the removal of an immigration chief have set a deadline for top civil servant Anson Chan to hand over a confidential report, a spokeswoman at Chan's office said on Saturday.
"Yes, we received an order last night and we are now seeking legal advice and we hope before the deadline we can give a reply to the select committee," the spokeswoman said by telephone.
"The deadline...is next Thursday, 5 p.m. (0900 GMT)" she said.
Chan refused in late April to hand over the report by the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC), saying it would harm the public interest and the future work of the ICAC.
The report formed the basis of a government decision to force immigration director Laurence Leung to retire last July after investigators found he had undisclosed business ties.
Chan has maintained that disclosure would set an unhealthy precedent for the anti-graft body and undermine its operations given the highly confidential nature of its work.

The select committee, a legislative panel looking into the issue, has decided to hire a high-powered British lawyer familiar with arguments over "public interest" immunity to determine whether the government is breaking the law by refusing to hand over the report.

If Chan again refuses to release the report, the panel will decide whether to press Attorney-General Jeremy Matthews to prosecute her for contempt of the committee, the South China Morning Post reported on Saturday.
Both the British colonial government and Leung have denied reports that Leung passed on secret information to China, which will regain sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1.
